walkthroughs.body_html: Key air pollutants include PM2.5 and PM10 particulates, nitrogen oxides (NOx), sulfur oxides (SOx), carbon monoxide, ground-level ozone and volatile organic compounds. They cause asthma, heart disease and lung cancer. PM2.5 is particularly harmful as it lodges deep in the lungs and crosses into the bloodstream.

Eutrophication occurs when nitrate and phosphate from fertilisers and sewage enter water bodies, fuelling algal blooms. When the algae die, decomposers consume oxygen, suffocating fish and invertebrates. Oil spills coat seabirds and shorelines. Heavy metals like mercury and lead bioaccumulate in food webs.

Point sources are easily traced single outlets such as factory pipes or sewage discharges; they are often regulated by permit. Diffuse sources include agricultural runoff, road runoff and atmospheric deposition over wide areas and are harder to control. Tackling both requires monitoring, regulation and changing land use practices.
